script: Is De Zerbi about to get SACKED soon? Tottenham spent over 300 million pounds this summer on players like Sandro Tonali and Paul van Hecke to push for Europe. And five games into the season, Spurs have zero wins, only three goals scored, and are sitting dead last in the Premier League in what is officially the worst start in the club's entire Premier League history. But this isn't the first time De Zerbi has found himself in this position. He got sacked at Palermo back in 2016, and then at Marseille after a Champions League exit to Club Brugge and a 5-0 loss to PSG, he left by mutual consent with reports saying that he'd completely lost the dressing room. So when Spurs hired him in March on a five-year deal as their third manager of the season, they needed him to keep them up and then rebuild from there. He did exactly that by picking up four points from the final three games to keep Spurs up, which earned him a full pre-season and 300 million pounds worth of new players. But the next season, things looked more or less the same for Tottenham. After the opening day 3-0 loss to Brentford, De Zerbi publicly called out his own defenders and Tonali for not being physically ready. Pundits immediately said he was shifting blame onto his players, and many people believe he is going to be the next Premier League manager sacked. While on top of this, Kieran McKenna, who's currently out of work, was spotted at a Spurs versus Everton game, which only added fuel. But the club's CEO did publicly back De Zerbi this week, so as of right now, he's safe. But their next league game is Coventry at home on October 17th, a team also sitting in the bottom three. And if Spurs can't start picking up wins soon, no amount of public backing is going to matter.
